note: Human labels: Spark team hand coding (sentence level). The judge is a model and can be wrong; it is scored here so its flags can be trusted to the measured degree. NDCG@10 is from the 2026-10-15 retrieval run, judged by AI, not by these human labels.

questions.label: green_labels.decreasing_emissions
questions.question: Which ads describe reducing or decreasing greenhouse gas emissions?

counts: The ad explicitly states that a product, service, action, or organization reduces, decreases, cuts, lowers, or otherwise limits greenhouse gas emissions.
The ad explicitly states that a product, service, action, or organization helps prevent, avoid, or eliminate greenhouse gas emissions.],
does_not_count: The ad only mentions greenhouse gas emissions, climate change, carbon neutrality, or sustainability without describing a reduction or decrease in emissions.
The ad describes reducing energy use, fuel use, pollution, or carbon emissions without indicating that the reduction concerns greenhouse gas emissions.
The ad makes a general environmental benefit claim without stating that greenhouse gas emissions are reduced or decreased.

questions.label: green_labels.policies_programs
questions.question: Which ads mention environmental or climate policies, regulations or programs?

counts: The ad’s text explicitly mentions an environmental or climate policy, regulation, or program.
The mention may refer to a specific or general government, institutional, or organizational policy, regulation, or program.
A statement about implementing, supporting, opposing, complying with, or benefiting from such a policy, regulation, or program counts.
does_not_count: General environmental or climate claims without mentioning a policy, regulation, or program.
Mentions of environmental conditions, impacts, or technologies that do not identify or refer to a policy, regulation, or program.
Policies, regulations, or programs unrelated to environmental or climate issues.

questions.label: ff_labels.infrastructure_and_production
questions.question: Which ads mention fossil fuel infrastructure or production, such as drilling, pipelines, refineries or power plants?

counts: The ad’s text mentions fossil fuel production activities or sites, such as drilling or extraction.
The ad’s text mentions fossil fuel infrastructure, such as pipelines, refineries, or power plants.
does_not_count: Mentions of fossil fuels only as a general energy source, without referring to production or infrastructure.
Mentions of unrelated infrastructure or energy facilities that are not associated with fossil fuels.

questions.label: green_labels.recycling_waste_management
questions.question: Which ads mention recycling or waste management?

counts: The ad’s text explicitly mentions recycling.
The ad’s text explicitly mentions waste management, such as managing, reducing, collecting, treating, or disposing of waste.
does_not_count: Ads that mention environmental protection or sustainability without mentioning recycling or waste management.
Ads that mention reusable, recyclable, or recycled products without referring to recycling as an activity or waste management.

questions.label: green_labels.nature_animal_references
questions.question: Which ads refer to nature or animals?

counts: The ad’s text explicitly refers to nature, such as the natural world, landscapes, plants, forests, rivers, or other nonhuman natural environments.
The ad’s text explicitly refers to animals or specific animal species.‌
does_not_count: An ad that uses imagery of nature or animals without referring to them in its text.
An ad that uses words such as “natural” only to describe a product, without referring to nature itself.
